### Inline comments

#### gemini-code-assist on `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/config-hook.mjs:45`

[View inline comment](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/pull/27346#discussion_r3566476443)

```diff
+ * Allow OpenCode to use aidevops-managed state and linked worktrees without
+ * repeatedly asking for external-directory approval. Keep the exception
+ * narrow: unrelated paths retain the user's existing permission policy.
+ * @param {object} config - OpenCode Config object (mutable)
+ * @returns {number} number of managed allow rules added or corrected
+ */
+export function registerManagedDirectoryPermissions(config) {
+  if (typeof config.permission === "string") {
+    config.permission = { external_directory: { "*": config.permission } };
+  } else if (!config.permission) {
+    config.permission = {};
+  }
```

> ![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)
> 
> When `config.permission` is a global string (e.g., `"ask"`), it acts as a default for all permission categories (such as `read` and `write`). Overwriting `config.permission` with an object that only contains `external_directory` will discard the global default for these other categories, potentially changing their behavior to OpenCode's internal defaults (or denying them). We should preserve the global default for other categories by explicitly copying it when converting the string to an object.

title: Keep issue-started interactive sessions local
body:
## Pre-flight

- Memory recall found no prior lesson matching this invariant.
- Discovery found related claim hardening but no open issue that forbids worker dispatch from an issue-started interactive session.
- Tier: `tier:standard`; the policy is decided, but entrypoint, routing, and regression tests must coordinate.

## What

Make issue-started interactive sessions authoritative local implementation contexts. They must bypass background/remote worker claims and implement in their linked worktree, even when the issue carries `auto-dispatch` or the local loop runs asynchronously.

## Why

An interactive user starts work on an issue because they cannot wait for a worker. Reinterpreting local `--background` execution as remote-worker intent wastes time, creates duplicate claims, and delays visible progress.

## Complete Write Surface

- `.agents/scripts/interactive-start-helper.sh` — establish an explicit local-only issue implementation marker and always claim auto-dispatch issues as `--implementing`.
- `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper-commands.sh` — preserve takeover semantics and fail closed on worker-claim routing.

title: bug: aidevops config commands recursively invoke config-helper main
body:
## Description

Every `aidevops config` subcommand fails before reaching the requested operation. Direct execution of `config-helper.sh` fails identically. The configuration helper sources `shared-constants.sh`, which sources `shared-feature-toggles.sh`, which sources `config-helper.sh` again. During that recursive source, the helper's direct-execution guard misclassifies the nested source as direct execution and calls `main` with the shared-module path as the command.

This makes the documented durable configuration surface unusable for `get`, `set`, `list`, `validate`, and related commands.

See-also: #27401

## Expected Behavior

`aidevops config get <dotpath>` should print the effective value, and `aidevops config set <dotpath> <value>` should persist the override without shell errors.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```bash
aidevops config get orchestration.min_worker_concurrency
```

**Actual output**:

```text
[ERROR] Unknown command: <agents-dir>/scripts/shared-feature-toggles.sh
config-helper.sh - Manage aidevops configuration (JSONC)
...
shared-constants.sh: line 1482: pop_var_context: head of shell_variables not a function context
```

**Expected output**:

```text
6
```

**Causal code**:

- `aidevops.sh:1175-1185` launches `config-helper.sh` as a new Bash process.
- `.agents/scripts/config-helper.sh:57-62` sources `shared-constants.sh` when the helper runs standalone.
- `.agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh:1479-1482` sources `shared-feature-toggles.sh` through `_source_shared_module_with_retry`.
- `.agents/scripts/shared-feature-toggles.sh:62-67` sources `config-helper.sh` again.
- `.agents/scripts/config-helper.sh:1151-1156` tests `BASH_SOURCE[0] == $0`; because the top-level executable is also `config-helper.sh`, this remains true during the recursive source and invokes `main` with the sourcing function's positional argument (`shared-feature-toggles.sh`) as the command.

The feature-toggle extraction originated in PR #20066 (`880ccb1e1`); the current source-retry call was introduced by `426051c1d`. The bug still reproduces on installed v3.32.64, and the six commits currently ahead on remote `main` do not touch the implicated files.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install aidevops v3.32.64 on Linux with Bash 5.x.
2. Run any documented config command, such as `aidevops config get orchestration.min_worker_concurrency`.
3. Observe that the nested helper treats the shared-module path as an unknown command and exits without returning the setting.

## Workarounds Applied

- Set `_SHARED_CONSTANTS_LOADED=1` while invoking `config-helper.sh` directly, which bypasses the recursive source sufficiently for `set` operations.
- This workaround is incomplete for commands such as `validate`, because skipping `shared-constants.sh` also omits dependencies including `_file_mtime_epoch`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- All documented `aidevops config` subcommands execute without recursive `main` invocation or `pop_var_context` errors.
- Direct execution and sourced-library use of `config-helper.sh` are both covered by regression tests.
- The fix does not reintroduce the ShellCheck source cycle or Bash 3.2/modern-Bash portability regressions described in the existing comments.
- A test verifies `get`, `set`, and `validate` through the public `aidevops config` entry point.

## Environment

- aidevops v3.32.64 (`cb027b6f6`)
- OpenCode
- Ubuntu 24.04 virtual machine
- Bash 5.x
- systemd 255

## Additional Context

No private repository names, usernames, local absolute paths, credentials, or configuration values are included. This report is separate from the schema/default drift issue because it affects command dispatch and dependency loading independently of schema contents.

title: bug: shipped foss defaults fail shipped config schema
body:
## Description

The shipped default configuration contains a top-level `foss` object, but the shipped JSON Schema does not define `foss` and rejects unknown top-level properties. Consequently, configuration validation rejects aidevops' own merged defaults even when the user's override file is valid.

This is a defaults/schema drift defect, independent of the separate `aidevops config` recursive dispatch failure.

See-also: #27400

## Expected Behavior

The shipped defaults must validate against the shipped schema. `aidevops config validate` should only fail for an invalid user or default configuration, not because a framework-owned default key is absent from the schema.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```bash
aidevops config validate
```

After bypassing the separate config command dispatch defect so validation can run, the validator reports:

**Actual output**:

```text
[OK] Defaults file is valid JSON
[OK] User config is valid JSON
Validation error: Additional properties are not allowed ('foss' was unexpected)
[ERROR] Config fails JSON Schema validation (see above)
```

**Expected output**:

```text
[OK] Defaults file is valid JSON
[OK] User config is valid JSON
[OK] Config passes JSON Schema validation
```

**Causal code**:

- `.agents/configs/aidevops.defaults.jsonc:170-188` defines top-level `foss.enabled`, `foss.max_daily_tokens`, and `foss.max_concurrent_contributions`.
- `.agents/configs/aidevops-config.schema.json:7-506` has no top-level `foss` property and ends with `additionalProperties: false`.
- `.agents/scripts/config-helper.sh:1009-1049` validates the merged default-plus-user configuration, so framework-owned schema drift necessarily fails every validation when a JSON Schema validator is available.

`foss` was added by PR #12304 (`4fc3a6be7`) on 2026-03-28. A history search found no corresponding schema addition. The bug still exists on installed v3.32.64, and the six commits currently ahead on remote `main` do not touch either config file.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install aidevops v3.32.64 with Python `jsonschema` or `ajv` available.
2. Run `aidevops config validate` after the separate config-dispatch defect is fixed or bypassed.
3. Observe that the framework's own `foss` default is rejected as an unknown property.

## Workarounds Applied

- Bypassed the separate recursive config command failure to reach `cmd_validate`.
- Treated the resulting `foss` rejection as framework schema drift rather than modifying or removing the user's valid worker-concurrency settings.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Add a schema definition for the shipped `foss` object, including types and sensible bounds for all three current fields.
- Add a regression test that strips JSONC comments, parses the complete shipped defaults, and validates them against the shipped schema.
- Ensure CI fails whenever future default keys and schema properties drift.
- `aidevops config validate` passes with defaults only and with a valid user override.

## Environment

- aidevops v3.32.64 (`cb027b6f6`)
- OpenCode
- Ubuntu 24.04 virtual machine
- Bash 5.x
- Python `jsonschema` installed

## Additional Context

No private repository names, usernames, local absolute paths, credentials, or user configuration values are included. This warrants a sibling issue rather than combining it with command dispatch because the schema defect remains after the command loader is repaired and has a distinct fix and regression test.

title: Git shim recursively selects runtime-bundle shims and saturates host after hot deploy
body:
## Description

The canonical Git shim can recursively select a different aidevops runtime-bundle Git shim as its `REAL_GIT` after a hot deployment. Long-running sessions retain an older immutable runtime bundle on `PATH`, while mutable deployed paths point to a newer bundle. Each generation excludes itself but does not exclude other runtime-bundle generations, producing an alternating Bash/Python process tree rather than reaching native Git.

This caused sustained host saturation without additional user workload: hundreds of short-lived shim/guard processes, approximately 28 related process spawns per second, 25–39 runnable tasks on an 8-vCPU host, 0% idle CPU, and load averages above 30. Normal Git metadata probes timed out and framework workers, pulse routines, review responders, and setup operations were degraded.

This is cross-platform in mechanism: Linux supplied the observed evidence, but any supported runtime with multiple aidevops shim generations ahead of native Git on `PATH` can recurse.

## Expected Behavior

The shim must resolve one immutable native Git executable and invoke at most one policy guard per user Git command. Deploying a newer aidevops runtime must remain safe for long-running sessions pinned to an older runtime bundle.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```bash
git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-dir
```

**Actual output**:

```text
subprocess.TimeoutExpired: Command '['<older-runtime-bundle>/agents/scripts/git',
'rev-parse', '--path-format=absolute', '--git-dir'] timed out after 5 seconds
```

During the timeout, the process tree alternates between generations:

```text
python3 <newer-bundle>/canonical-git-command-guard.py
└─ bash <older-bundle>/agents/scripts/git rev-parse ...
   └─ python3 <older-bundle>/canonical-git-command-guard.py
      └─ bash <newer-bundle>/agents/scripts/git rev-parse ...
         └─ ...
```

Observed bounded sampling:

- 8 logical CPUs; load approximately 33/32/27
- 25–39 runnable tasks; 0% CPU idle across repeated samples
- approximately 125 live canonical guards and 114 live Git shims
- 145 guard and 133 shim spawns in 10 seconds (approximately 27.8 combined spawns/second)
- individual descendants were 0–5 seconds old, but populations remained stable because new callers and recursive descendants replaced timed-out processes
- memory, disk, OOM, provider throttling, and GitHub quota exhaustion were not the limiting resources

**Blocked child command**:

```text
<other-runtime-bundle>/agents/scripts/git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-dir
```

**Backend state**:

No remote backend is involved in the reproducer. The blocked child and recursive process ancestry were captured locally. Native `/usr/bin/git` was present but was never reached by affected chains.

**Expected output**:

The repository Git directory should be returned promptly, with process depth limited to one shim, one guard, and one native Git child.

**Causal code**:

```text
b941a51749e8104e1b0c802fd0a8aad8238101b4 introduced the Git shim.
54900c3b9f113d119d44eb6c76296bf753e07452 added exclusions that do not cover runtime-bundle paths.
48a522d01 introduced/preserved immutable runtime-bundle paths for live sessions, activating the latent resolver assumption across generations.
```

Current relevant implementation:

- `.agents/scripts/git:16-29` searches `which -a git` and excludes only the current file plus `*/.aidevops/agents/scripts/git` and `*/.agents/scripts/git`.
- It does not exclude `*/.aidevops/runtime-bundles/*/agents/scripts/git` or `*/.aidevops/bin/git` by resolved identity.
- `.agents/scripts/canonical_git_policy.py:60-88` invokes the selected `real_git_path` for two five-second `rev-parse` probes; selecting another shim recursively re-enters the guard.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a long-running OpenCode session whose `PATH` begins with runtime bundle generation A.
2. Deploy aidevops generation B so mutable deployed shim paths resolve to B while the session retains A.
3. Ensure both generation A and generation B Git shims precede native Git in `which -a git` output.
4. Run any Git command that enters the canonical guard, such as `git rev-parse --git-dir`.
5. Observe alternating A/B shim and guard descendants until timeout; concurrent framework callers sustain a process storm.

## Workarounds Applied

- Used `/usr/bin/git` explicitly for read-only diagnosis and remediation commands.
- Ran diagnostic helpers with a sanitized system-only `PATH`.
- Avoided ordinary wrapped Git commands after confirming the recursion.
- Did not use broad `pkill` commands because they could terminate unrelated Python/Bash sessions.

These are containment measures only; long-running automation still needs a framework-level fix.

## Recommended Fix Considerations

1. Resolve native Git deterministically at deployment time or through a trusted immutable system path. Do not use `which -a git` from inside the shim as the primary downstream resolver.
2. Reject every aidevops shim location by resolved path, including runtime bundles, mutable deployed paths, repository shims, and `~/.aidevops/bin/git`.
3. Add a recursion sentinel environment variable so guard re-entry fails closed immediately rather than spawning another generation.
4. Catch `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` in `_git_output()` and return a controlled policy failure without a traceback.
5. Restart or safely refresh long-running runtime sessions after deployment when their pinned environment can conflict with mutable executable paths.
6. Extend process-runaway detection to identify high-rate short-lived shim/guard churn; age-only detection reported no runaway process during this incident.
7. Avoid hard-coding `/usr/bin/git` without a portable resolver: macOS may require `xcrun --find git`, and other supported environments may place native Git elsewhere.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A test places two distinct runtime-bundle Git shims before native Git on `PATH`; either generation always resolves native Git and never the other shim.
- One Git invocation creates at most one shim and one guard process before native Git.
- A stale session pinned to generation A remains safe after generation B activates.
- Recursive re-entry fails immediately and emits a bounded diagnostic.
- Linux and macOS native-Git resolution paths are covered.
- Existing canonical-main mutation protections continue to pass.
- A bounded stress test confirms process count and spawn rate remain stable during concurrent Git probes.

## Environment

- aidevops versions involved: 3.32.61–3.32.65; current diagnostics reported 3.32.65
- OpenCode with long-running immutable runtime-bundle sessions
- Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- bash 5.2.21
- GitHub CLI 2.96.0
- 8-vCPU virtualized host

## Additional Context

The latent resolver defect appears to date from the July 11 Git-shim changes, while immutable runtime-bundle/session pinning made cross-generation selection possible. The earliest directly verified recursive timeout in the observing environment occurred after multiple same-day hot deployments. Heavy workload was not required: startup hooks, pulse, workers, setup, and repository discovery issue Git probes automatically.

The five-second subprocess timeout bounds each ancestor but does not bound descendants or independent callers. It therefore limits individual waits while still allowing sustained replacement and full host saturation.

title: Make full-loop dual-mode execution efficient and observable
body:
## Pre-flight

- Existing issue #27389 owns local/CI gate parity and evidence reuse.
- Existing issue #27392 owns interactive versus headless release authorization and merge-only completion.
- Existing roadmap #27145 owns durable cross-session task coordination, not within-session orchestration.
- No matching open issue was found for bounded subagent decomposition, event-driven PR convergence, and phase-level performance budgets.
- Tier: `tier:thinking`; this changes orchestration policy shared by interactive and background execution.

## What

Make full-loop execution fast and predictable in both interactive sessions and background workers by sharing one deterministic lifecycle engine while applying mode-specific interaction policy, bounded parallel subagents, event-driven PR convergence, and phase-level performance telemetry.

## Why

PR #27414 completed correctly but required serial exploration, implementation, repeated adversarial reviews, fixed-duration CI polling, multiple repair pushes, and manual lifecycle resumption. The implementation work was not the dominant cost. Full-loop needs to eliminate duplicated agent work and idle waits without weakening safety gates.

## Scope boundaries

This issue owns orchestration and observability only:

- Do not duplicate the gate contracts in #27389.
- Do not duplicate release authorization in #27392.
- Do not redesign cross-machine task identity or publication from #27145.
- Keep deterministic lifecycle transitions in scripts; keep decomposition, prioritization, and review judgment in models.

## Complete Write Surface

- `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md` — dual-mode lifecycle and progress contract.
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh`, `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-state.sh`, `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh` — resumable executor, terminal-check waiting, and lifecycle evidence.
- `.agents/scripts/task-decompose-helper.sh` — bounded decomposition output suitable for within-session dispatch.
- `.agents/reference/agent-routing.md` — subagent ownership, model tier, concurrency, and deduplication rules.
- `.agents/reference/observability.md` — phase timings, retries, agent/tool cost, and efficiency budgets.
- Full-loop, headless runtime, merge-gate, decomposition, and observability tests.

## Execution contract

### Shared lifecycle engine

1. Use one persisted state machine for interactive and headless execution.
2. `start --background` must either launch an executor that demonstrably advances state or return a machine-readable `initialized-only` result; never imply progress when no worker is running.
3. Every phase records start/end time, attempts, terminal evidence, and next safe resume action.

### Interactive policy

1. Keep the primary agent responsive and on the critical path.
2. Dispatch only bounded, non-overlapping subagents with the lowest sufficient effort tier.
3. Run long checks/waits asynchronously when supported and surface state transitions rather than fixed sleep narration.

### Background/headless policy

1. Never prompt; resume from persisted evidence after runtime interruption.
2. Use the same decomposition plan and lifecycle transitions, but permit autonomous repair within brief scope.
3. Enforce global and per-task subagent concurrency limits so parallel work does not exhaust machine resources.

## Subagent efficiency

1. Produce a task graph with explicit ownership of files/questions and dependencies.
2. Parallelize only independent discovery, implementation, test, or review units.
3. Prevent the primary agent from repeating delegated exploration unless evidence is missing or contradictory.
4. Consolidate adversarial review into parallel specialties—correctness/concurrency, security/trust, compatibility/quality, and test adequacy—then perform one repair pass.
5. Prefer cheap models for bounded discovery and mechanical verification; reserve thinking models for architecture and cross-finding synthesis.
6. Record reused context and outputs so retries do not relaunch completed subagents.

## Event-driven PR convergence

1. Treat pending checks as pending, never as failures.
2. Wait with bounded adaptive backoff or provider events, keyed to the exact PR head.
3. On terminal failure, retrieve only failing required-check evidence and map it to the canonical local command from #27389.
4. Repair, push, and resume automatically within iteration/resource budgets.
5. Stop only for a genuine authority, security, architectural, secret, or exhausted-budget blocker.

## Performance evidence

Record per full-loop run:

- Wall time and active compute by lifecycle phase.
- Primary-agent and subagent calls by tier, duration, retries, and outcome.
- Duplicate/delegated work avoided.
- Local preflight, CI wait, terminal repair, release, and cleanup time.
- Safety-gate false positives and manual-resume count.

Default budgets should be configurable by mode and task tier. Budget exhaustion creates a durable continuation checkpoint; it never marks incomplete acceptance criteria complete.

## Verification

- Add an interactive fixture proving the primary remains responsive while bounded subagents and CI waits run.
- Add a headless fixture proving autonomous resume after termination with no duplicated subagent work.
- Add a decomposition fixture with two independent units and one dependent unit; assert bounded parallelism and no overlapping file ownership.
- Add a PR-check fixture covering pending → failure → repair → new head → success, with no fixed-duration polling assumptions.
- Add an `initialized-only` regression for background start when no executor was launched.
- Add telemetry assertions for phase duration, attempt count, subagent reuse, and terminal lifecycle state.
- Run full-loop state/merge tests, headless runtime tests, agent routing validation, ShellCheck, and framework lint.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Interactive and background modes share lifecycle mechanics but enforce distinct interaction policies.
- [ ] Background start never reports a running loop without a live advancing executor.
- [ ] Independent subagent work runs concurrently within configured resource limits; overlapping work remains serialized.
- [ ] Completed delegated work is reused across retries and resumptions.
- [ ] Pending CI causes no repair action; terminal required failures trigger focused evidence and autonomous repair.
- [ ] No fixed sleep is required for normal PR convergence.
- [ ] Every run emits phase timing and agent-efficiency evidence suitable for regression tracking.
- [ ] Safety, review, release authorization, and cleanup gates remain fail-closed.

## Dependencies

- Related: #27145 for durable task coordination.
- Integrate with #27389 for canonical local/CI gate decisions.
- Integrate with #27392 for mode-aware release/deploy authorization.

## Recoverability

Land the persisted executor/status contract first, then subagent planning, then event-driven convergence, then telemetry. Each phase must retain compatibility with the current synchronous path until its regression fixtures pass. Create WIP commits after focused tests and before broad framework gates.

## Seeded Draft PR

Not created: this requires orchestration design across moving lifecycle code, so an untested seed would over-constrain the worker.

## PR Conventions

Use `Resolves #NNN` for the final leaf implementation. If decomposed into child issues, use `For #NNN` on intermediate PRs and keep this issue open until all acceptance criteria are verified.

Additionally, when using a while-read loop that handles missing trailing newlines, ensure to check if the line is non-empty inside the loop body to avoid processing empty lines.

```shell
	local attempts="${DLW_SYSTEMD_STABILITY_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
	local wait_i=0 stable_count=0 snapshot="" main_pid="" active_state="" sub_state=""
	local exec_main_code="" exec_main_status="" result="" key="" value=""

	[[ "$attempts" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || attempts=3
	[[ "$poll_seconds" =~ ^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$ ]] || poll_seconds="0.2"

	while [[ "$wait_i" -lt "$attempts" ]]; do
		snapshot=$(_dlw_systemd_snapshot "$unit_name" "$state_file")
		main_pid=""
		active_state=""
		sub_state=""
		exec_main_code="" exec_main_status="" result=""
		while IFS='=' read -r key value || [[ -n "$key" ]]; do
			[[ -n "$key" ]] || continue
			case "$key" in
				MainPID) main_pid="$value" ;;
				ActiveState) active_state="$value" ;;
				SubState) sub_state="$value" ;;
				ExecMainCode) exec_main_code="$value" ;;
				ExecMainStatus) exec_main_status="$value" ;;
				Result) result="$value" ;;
			esac
		done <<<"$snapshot"

		if [[ "$active_state" == "failed" || "$active_state" == "inactive" ]]; then
			printf 'LaunchState=startup_failed\n' >>"$state_file"
			echo "[dispatch_worker_launch] systemd startup_failed unit=${unit_name} issue=${issue_number} MainPID=${main_pid:-0} ExecMainCode=${exec_main_code:-unknown} ExecMainStatus=${exec_main_status:-unknown} Result=${result:-unknown} state=${active_state:-unknown}/${sub_state:-unknown}" >>"$LOGFILE"
			return 2
		fi

		if [[ "$main_pid" == "$expected_pid" && "$active_state" == "active" && "$sub_state" == "running" ]]; then
			stable_count=$((stable_count + 1))
		else
			stable_count=0
		fi
		wait_i=$((wait_i + 1))
		[[ "$stable_count" -ge "$attempts" ]] && {
			printf 'LaunchState=worker_ready\n' >>"$state_file"
			return 0
		}
		sleep "$poll_seconds"
	done

	printf 'LaunchState=pid_observed\n' >>"$state_file"
	return 1

title: Merged-PR reconciliation recloses recurrent file-size debt from obsolete completion evidence
body:
## Description

Recurrent file-size debt can enter a deterministic close/reopen loop. The large-file gate correctly reopens a previously completed canonical debt issue when the current file has grown back above the configured threshold. Generic merged-PR reconciliation then closes that issue again using the historical PR that resolved the earlier occurrence, without revalidating the current file state.

This creates contradictory issue state, repeated API writes/comments, and stale completion labels. The consumer repository and target path are intentionally omitted.

## Expected Behavior

Historical completion evidence should remain valid only for the occurrence it resolved. If the current cited file is again at or above the threshold, generic reconciliation must not close the reopened debt issue from the old merged PR.

## Reproducer

**Observed sequence**:

1. Create a `file-size-debt` issue for a file above the threshold.
2. Merge a closing PR that reduces the file below the threshold.
3. Later commits grow the same file above the threshold again.
4. Allow the large-file gate to reopen the canonical debt issue.
5. Run merged-PR reconciliation.
6. Observe the reopened issue close from the historical PR, then reopen again on a later large-file-gate pass.

**Actual output/state**:

```text
Closed by the original resolving PR
Reopened after current line-count validation
Closed by reconciliation using the historical merged PR
Reopened after current line-count validation
...repeats across pulse cycles
```

The observed consumer issue had six automated close/reopen cycles. After a manual close, it reopened again because the current file remained above threshold, confirming that reopening—not closure—was the correct current state.

**Expected output/state**:

```text
The recurrent debt issue remains open while the current file exceeds the threshold.
Historical merged-PR evidence does not close the new occurrence.
```

**Causal code**:

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-large-file-gate.sh:330-369` revalidates the current line count and deliberately reopens recurrent debt.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-close.sh:200-275` closes open issues from merged-PR references without an equivalent current debt-outcome check.

## Workarounds Applied

- Manually inspected the issue timeline to separate legitimate recurrence from stale completion evidence.
- Manually closed the issue once; the large-file gate correctly reopened it because the debt still existed. This workaround is not durable and should not be repeated.

## Considerations

- Reuse the existing large-file outcome verifier rather than duplicating threshold logic.
- Preserve generic reconciliation for genuinely orphaned issue closures.
- Scope recurrence identity by issue type and cited path so unrelated issue classes are unaffected.
- Clear or supersede stale `solved:*`/completion labels when a canonical debt issue legitimately recurs.
- Ensure the fix is idempotent and does not create a new issue for every recurrence.
- Add an integration regression covering: resolve below threshold → regress above threshold → reopen → merged-PR reconciliation → remains open.
- Consider whether historical closing references need occurrence/version metadata rather than being treated as permanent completion proof.

## Environment

- aidevops v3.32.76
- Linux
- OpenCode runtime

## Additional Context

Related completed work already validates current file size before reopening recurrent debt. No matching issue was found for the inverse path where generic reconciliation recloses the valid recurrence from obsolete completion evidence.

title: Enhancement: preserve bounded offline context for URL-only worker recovery
body:
## Description

Evaluate preserving a bounded, sanitized, durable issue-body snapshot for workers launched in URL-only fallback mode.

After repeated zero-artifact worker attempts, `_dlw_prepare_prompt_for_launch` intentionally replaces the embedded brief with a minimal prompt that instructs the worker to read the issue through `gh issue view`. This protects against malformed, oversized, or unsafe embedded prompts. In observed Linux worker runs, however, authenticated GitHub reads repeatedly timed out. Because URL-only mode deliberately removed the embedded brief and no durable local snapshot remained, recovery could not determine the task and correctly stopped without changes.

This report is an enhancement proposal, not a claim that the current fail-safe is incorrect. Maintainers should decide whether offline resilience is worth the additional trust, storage, freshness, and prompt-complexity costs.

## Expected Behavior

When live GitHub reads are unavailable, a URL-only worker could optionally recover enough trusted task context to make a safe decision—or produce a precise blocker—without restoring the original unbounded prompt.

## Observed Scenario

1. Repeated no-artifact evidence triggers URL-only fallback.
2. The generated prompt retains repository identity, issue number, and title, but excludes the original brief.
3. Worker-side `gh issue view`, REST reads, auth checks, and rate-limit probes time out.
4. Temporary seed context has already been cleaned and the branch contains no issue-specific artifact.
5. Brief recovery cannot proceed safely and releases the task without implementation.

Relevant implementation:

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh:523-540` defines the URL-only bootstrap.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh:585-595` replaces the original prompt after the fallback threshold.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-zero-output-url-fallback.sh:73-81` explicitly verifies that the full embedded brief is absent.

## Rationale

The existing design assumes live GitHub is the durable source of truth. A transient worker-environment or transport failure can therefore make URL-only recovery impossible even when dispatch already fetched enough issue metadata to identify the task. A bounded fallback artifact could reduce repeated no-work loops while retaining the security purpose of clean-room launch.

## Design Considerations

- Preserve URL-only mode's primary safety goal: never re-inject unbounded comments, generated HTML, audit chatter, or the original malformed prompt.
- Prefer a body-only, size-limited, sanitized snapshot with issue number, title, acceptance criteria, and source revision/timestamp.
- Treat the snapshot as fallback evidence, not fresher authority than GitHub. Workers should try the live issue first.
- Mark snapshot age and provenance so the worker can refuse stale or mismatched context.
- Store it in the worker's durable recovery area with strict permissions and cleanup rules.
- Keep prompt-injection scanning and collaborator trust checks in the snapshot-production path.
- Avoid embedding private repository names, local paths, credentials, or comment content in telemetry and public diagnostics.
- Consider a simpler alternative: retain the snapshot only for a blocker dossier and deterministic retry, not autonomous implementation.
- Distinguish literal runtime zero output from a worker that produced a blocker but no durable code artifact; this may be an observability concern rather than part of this enhancement.
- Validate continuation launches still receive `WORKER_ISSUE_NUMBER`; current v3.32.76 appears to address that separate older-runtime defect.

## Possible Acceptance Criteria

- URL-only mode continues to exclude the original full embedded prompt.
- Dispatch preserves a bounded, sanitized body snapshot with provenance.
- If live issue retrieval times out, recovery can consume the snapshot or emit a precise stale-context blocker.
- Tests cover GitHub timeout, stale snapshot, identity mismatch, malicious/unbounded body content, and normal live-read success.
- Maintainers can reject this proposal if the added trust/storage surface outweighs reduced no-work retries.

## Environment

- aidevops v3.32.76
- Linux systemd workers
- OpenCode runtime

## Additional Context

The existing URL-only behavior originated as a safeguard against repeated zero-output launches. This proposal should complement that safeguard, not undo it.

The `sha3()` function is an extension function in SQLite and is **not** built-in or available by default in standard SQLite command-line installations (such as the default `/usr/bin/sqlite3` on macOS or standard package manager builds on Ubuntu/Debian). Running this will result in a runtime error: `Error: no such function: sha3`.

Since this is a Node.js script, you should compute the hash in Node.js using the built-in `node:crypto` module (which you already import) and pass the pre-computed hash to the SQL query, or rely on SQLite's transactional ACID guarantees and `json_valid()` constraint to ensure integrity without needing a custom database-side hash.

<!-- provenance:start -->

<!-- provenance:end -->

### HIGH: gemini (gemini-code-assist[bot])
**File**: `.agents/scripts/task-coordinator.mjs:308`
![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

Using `renameSync(staged, target)` to overwrite an active SQLite database file while other processes might have it open is highly unsafe:
1. On Windows, `renameSync` will fail with `EBUSY` or permission denied if any other process has the database file open.
2. On Unix-like systems, other processes that currently have the database open will keep their file descriptors pointing to the unlinked old file. They will continue reading and writing to the old database, while new processes will open the new database file, leading to a split-brain state and silent data loss.
3. Deleting the `-wal` and `-shm` files of an active database can corrupt active connections.

Instead of unlinking and renaming the file, you should use SQLite's built-in `.restore` command to safely overwrite the target database. This leverages SQLite's own locking and journaling mechanisms to safely replace the database content without breaking active file descriptors.

```suggestion
sqlite(target, ".restore " + sqlEscape(staged) + "\n");
rmSync(staged, { force: true });
secureFile(target);
```

title: _rest_issue_list: --argjson next fails with Argument list too long on large issue bodies
body:
## Description

`_rest_issue_list()` in `shared-gh-wrappers-rest-fallback.sh` passes the entire raw API response via `--argjson next "$raw_page"` to jq. When `gh api /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues` returns issues with large bodies (e.g., review-followup issues containing full PR review summaries, multi-page diff fences), the JSON payload exceeds `ARG_MAX` (~2MB on Linux). jq exits with "Argument list too long" and the function returns exit code 1.

This causes `gh_issue_list` to fail for any repo that has open issues with large bodies. Downstream, pulse's `list_dispatchable_issue_candidates` sees an empty candidate list (`issue_json="[]"`) and never dispatches any issue from that repo.

## Expected Behavior

`_rest_issue_list()` should handle arbitrarily large API responses by piping data through stdin instead of passing it via `--argjson` command-line arguments.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```bash
AIDEVOPS_GH_REST_FIRST_READS=1 gh_issue_list --repo <webapp> --state open --json number,title --limit 100
```

**Actual output**:

```
[INFO] gh-wrapper: REST-first read mode, routing issue list to REST
<home>/.aidevops/agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-rest-fallback.sh: line 1446: /usr/bin/jq: Argument list too long
EXIT: 1
```

(Works with `--limit 5` because the response is small enough.)

**Expected output**: Valid JSON array of issues, exit code 0.

**Causal code**: `_rest_issue_list()` at line 1444-1446 of `shared-gh-wrappers-rest-fallback.sh`:

```bash
raw_count=$(printf '%s' "$raw_page" | jq 'length' 2>/dev/null) || return 1
combined=$(jq -cn --argjson prior "$combined" --argjson next "$raw_page" \
    '$prior + [$next[] | select(.pull_request == null)]') || return 1
```

`--argjson next "$raw_page"` embeds the full REST response (all fields including `body`, `user`, `reactions`, `labels`, etc.) as a CLI argument. For repos like <webapp> where review-followup issues contain large bodies (PR diffs, review summaries), a single page of 100 issues can exceed `ARG_MAX`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have a repo with open issues that have large bodies (e.g., auto-generated review-followup issues with embedded PR descriptions and diffs).
2. Run `gh_issue_list` with `AIDEVOPS_GH_REST_FIRST_READS=1` and `--limit` >= 100.
3. Observe `jq: Argument list too long` and exit code 1.

## Workarounds Applied

**Disable REST-first reads** as temporary workaround for pulse:

```bash
export AIDEVOPS_PULSE_REST_FIRST_READS=0
```

This causes `pulse-wrapper.sh:1657-1659` to skip setting `AIDEVOPS_GH_REST_FIRST_READS=1`, falling back to GraphQL for issue listing. Applied manually during the observing session to restore auto-dispatch.

An alternative workaround is to use `--limit 5` (small pages), but that makes the function useless for full enumeration.

## Siblings

- `pulse-check.log` shows a quoting bug: `pulse-check-helper.sh apply: No such file or directory` -- the call site treats `" apply"` as part of the path. Should be filed as a separate issue.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.32.82
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **gh CLI**: 2.89.0 (2026-03-26)

## Additional Context

The `--argjson` call accumulates data across pagination loops -- `$prior` grows with each page, so the failure becomes more likely on page 2+ when `$combined` doubles in size. Even page 1 can fail if the response is large enough.

Only `_rest_issue_list` is affected. `_rest_issue_search` and `_rest_pr_list` should be audited for the same pattern.

Suggested fix: pipe `$raw_page` through jq stdin instead of `--argjson`:

```bash
combined=$(printf '%s' "$raw_page" | jq -cn --argjson prior "$combined" '[$prior[]] + [$raw_page[] | select(.pull_request == null)]')
```

Or bypass jq accumulation entirely by writing pages to a temp file and merging at the end.

	if [[ ! -f "$helper" ]]; then

	if [[ -z "$default_branch" || "$default_branch" == "HEAD" ]]; then

	base_ref=$(git merge-base HEAD "origin/${default_branch:-main}" 2>/dev/null || git merge-base HEAD "${default_branch:-main}" 2>/dev/null || true)
	if [[ -z "$base_ref" ]]; then
		print_error "${metric}: merge-base unavailable; required result is incomplete"
		return 2
	fi

title: Fix coordinator artifact restore and postflight gate deterministically
body:
## Root cause

Release postflight for v3.32.85 failed after `forge-coordinator-state-helper.sh restore` returned several artifact IDs separated by newlines and interpolated the complete output into one GitHub artifact URL. The resulting URL contained control characters and `gh` rejected it.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/forge-coordinator-state-helper.sh`
- Postflight and coordinator restore tests under `.agents/scripts/tests/`
- Postflight workflow/JQ classification only if tests prove the gate also needs correction

## Reference pattern

Model artifact selection on other helpers that parse GitHub API arrays into one validated scalar before URL construction. Preserve fail-closed behavior for malformed responses.

## How

1. Parse artifact API results structurally rather than as newline-delimited scalar output.
2. Select exactly one newest valid checkpoint using deterministic ordering and repository/run identity constraints.
3. Distinguish no artifact, ambiguous/malformed evidence, and transient API failure.
4. Ensure postflight does not treat cancelled superseded evidence as the current terminal result.

## Verification

- Add fixtures for multiple artifacts, pagination, missing artifacts, malformed IDs, cancelled superseded runs, and one valid newest checkpoint.
- Run the focused coordinator restore and postflight tests.
- Run ShellCheck on changed shell files.
- Run framework lint in changed mode.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Restore constructs a URL from exactly one validated artifact ID.
- [ ] Multiple historical checkpoints select the newest eligible checkpoint deterministically.
- [ ] Malformed or ambiguous API output fails with actionable evidence and never reaches URL interpolation.
- [ ] Postflight passes when required current checks pass and historical/superseded runs are non-blocking.
- [ ] Regression tests cover the v3.32.85 failure mode.

title: gh shim recursively selects another aidevops shim after hot deploy
body:
## Description

The aidevops `gh` shim can recursively select a different aidevops `gh` shim as its downstream executable when a long-running session has an immutable runtime-bundle shim and the mutable installed shim both ahead of native GitHub CLI on `PATH`.

Each shim excludes only its own directory in `_find_real_gh()`. The runtime-bundle shim therefore selects the installed shim, while the installed shim selects the runtime-bundle shim. Even `gh --version` then alternates between the two wrappers until an external timeout kills the chain. GitHub is never contacted.

This is the `gh` equivalent of the cross-generation Git-shim defect fixed by #27405 / PR #27410, but that fix changed only the Git shim and canonical Git policy. It did not harden `.agents/scripts/gh`.

The failure blocks issue reads, claims, PR operations, diagnostics, pulse routines, and any framework helper that invokes ordinary `gh`. It initially resembles GitHub rate limiting, but direct API and native-CLI checks show healthy connectivity and ample quota.

## Expected Behavior

The shim must resolve one trusted native GitHub CLI executable and invoke it after at most one aidevops shim. Hot deployment must remain safe for long-running sessions pinned to an older immutable runtime bundle.

The documented `AIDEVOPS_GH_SHIM_DISABLE=1` bypass must always reach native `gh`, even when multiple aidevops shim generations are present on `PATH`.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```bash
/usr/bin/time -f 'elapsed=%e exit=%x' timeout 3s env \
  PATH=<runtime-bundle>/agents/scripts:<installed-aidevops>/agents/scripts:/usr/bin:/bin \
  gh --version
```

**Actual output**:

```text
Command exited with non-zero status 124
elapsed=3.00 exit=124
```

The same timeout occurs with the documented bypass:

```bash
timeout 3s env AIDEVOPS_GH_SHIM_DISABLE=1 \
  PATH=<runtime-bundle>/agents/scripts:<installed-aidevops>/agents/scripts:/usr/bin:/bin \
  gh --version
```

Control cases isolate the two-wrapper interaction:

```text
runtime-bundle shim + native gh: exit 0 in 0.08s
installed shim + native gh:      exit 0 in 0.08s
both shims + native gh:          exit 124 after 3.00s
/usr/bin/gh api rate_limit:      4,958/5,000 REST requests remaining
direct api.github.com request:   HTTP 200 in approximately 0.15s
```

**Blocked child command**:

```text
<other-aidevops-shim>/agents/scripts/gh --version
```

Resolution alternates by generation:

```text
runtime-bundle gh
  -> installed gh
    -> runtime-bundle gh
      -> installed gh
        -> repeats until timeout
```

**Backend state**:

GitHub is not the blocker. DNS and direct HTTPS connectivity were healthy, native `/usr/bin/gh` returned immediately, and the authenticated REST pool had 4,958 of 5,000 requests remaining.

**Expected output**:

```text
gh version 2.96.0 (2026-07-02)
```

The command should complete promptly and execute native GitHub CLI exactly once.

**Causal code**:

- `.agents/scripts/gh:165-181`: `_find_real_gh()` excludes only `_SHIM_DIR`, then accepts the first other executable named `gh` on `PATH`. It does not reject other runtime-bundle, mutable installed, repository, or aidevops bin shims by resolved identity.
- `.agents/scripts/gh:381-388`: ordinary passthrough commands resolve and `exec` the incorrectly selected wrapper before the later recursion guard is reached.
- `.agents/scripts/gh:395-400`: the emergency bypass uses the same defective resolver, so it also recurses.
- `.agents/scripts/gh:407-409`: the recursion guard again calls `_find_real_gh()`; with two generations it forwards to the other shim instead of native `gh`.

The deployed `gh` shim was byte-identical across aidevops v3.32.61, v3.32.70, v3.32.87, and the mutable installed copy. The defect is therefore latent rather than introduced by PR #27410. Immutable runtime bundles and hot deployment activate the invalid assumption that “not this shim” means “native GitHub CLI,” matching the architectural failure identified in #27405.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a long-running session whose `PATH` begins with an immutable runtime-bundle `agents/scripts` directory.
2. Keep the mutable installed `agents/scripts` directory later on `PATH`, before native GitHub CLI.
3. Confirm both locations contain the aidevops `gh` shim.
4. Run `gh --version`, `gh auth status`, or any GitHub operation.
5. Observe timeout with both shims, while either shim alone reaches native `gh` immediately.
6. Repeat with `AIDEVOPS_GH_SHIM_DISABLE=1`; observe that the documented bypass also times out.

## Workarounds Applied

- Invoked `/usr/bin/gh` directly for bounded read-only diagnosis and GitHub API checks.
- Used a sanitized `PATH` containing only one aidevops `gh` shim plus system binaries when shim behavior was required.
- Added external `timeout` bounds to prevent recursive calls from hanging the session indefinitely.
- Avoided attributing the symptom to rate limiting until direct quota and transport checks disproved it.

These are containment measures. Framework helpers and long-running automation still call ordinary `gh` and remain vulnerable.

## Recommended Fix Considerations

1. Reuse the trusted-native-executable strategy and cross-generation identity rejection developed for #27405, adapted for GitHub CLI.
2. Reject every aidevops-managed `gh` candidate by canonical/resolved identity, including immutable runtime bundles, mutable installed paths, repository shims, and aidevops bin paths.
3. Add an immediate recursion sentinel that fails closed with a bounded diagnostic rather than invoking another candidate wrapper.
4. Ensure the emergency bypass resolves native `gh` without entering instrumentation, signature, privacy, or normal resolver paths that can recurse.
5. Preserve portability: do not assume `/usr/bin/gh` is the only valid native location. Homebrew and other supported installations need a trusted resolution path.
6. Treat instrumentation as fail-open, but do not let fail-open behavior select another policy shim.
7. Consider a shared native-tool resolver for `git`, `gh`, and future PATH shims so this defect class cannot recur independently in each wrapper.
8. Keep hot-deployed immutable sessions supported; requiring users to restart every session would reduce exposure but would not correct executable identity.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A test places two distinct aidevops `gh` shim generations before native `gh` on `PATH`; either entry shim invokes native `gh` exactly once without recursion.
- A test covers runtime-bundle, mutable installed, repository, bin, and symlinked shim candidates.
- `AIDEVOPS_GH_SHIM_DISABLE=1` reaches native `gh` with multiple generations present.
- Recursive re-entry exits immediately with a bounded, actionable diagnostic.
- Ordinary passthrough commands such as `gh --version` and intercepted commands such as `gh issue view` are both covered.
- Existing signature injection, privacy scanning, headless write protection, read rewriting, and API instrumentation tests continue to pass.
- Linux and macOS/Homebrew native-resolution fixtures are covered.
- A bounded concurrent test confirms stable process depth and count after hot-deployment-style PATH composition.

## Environment

- aidevops v3.32.87 (latest observed during diagnostics: v3.32.88)
- OpenCode interactive session with immutable runtime-bundle paths
- Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- bash 5.2.21
- GitHub CLI 2.96.0

## Additional Context

This is not Linux-specific in mechanism. Linux supplied the reproducer, but the resolver and recursion behavior are Bash/PATH-based. Any supported platform can trigger it when two aidevops shim identities precede native `gh`.

Related: #27405 established the same invariant for Git: “not this shim” is not sufficient proof that a candidate is native. PR #27410 fixed that specific Git path and was released in v3.32.70. This report requests the equivalent correction for `gh`, with consideration for consolidating native executable resolution so future shims inherit the invariant.

analysis.

the bot's finding is real, but the fix requires a decision that is
architectural, policy, breaking-change, or otherwise genuinely outside

ready-to-approve recommendation, not a blank task.

> thinking and delivers a recommendation. Only escalate what is genuinely
> a maintainer-only decision.

### Inline comments

#### gemini-code-assist on `.agents/scripts/memory/maintenance-prune.sh:94`

[View inline comment](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/pull/27370#discussion_r3566608712)

```diff
@@ -89,6 +89,9 @@ cmd_prune() {
 		log_info "Hard age retention applies before relevance judgment; accessed records cannot escape the age bound"
 	fi
 	_prune_flat_threshold "$older_than_days" "$dry_run"

+		_prune_ai_judged "$older_than_days" "$dry_run" false

```

> ![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

> The `_prune_ai_judged` function is fragile and prone to parsing failures when processing memory content that contains newlines or pipe (`|`) characters.
> 
> In `_prune_ai_judged`, the query results are read using `while IFS='|' read -r mem_id mem_type mem_confidence mem_content age_days accessed_flag; do`. Since the default output format of `sqlite3` is pipe-separated, any newline or pipe character in `mem_content` (which is `substr(l.content, 1, 300)`) will cause the `read` command to split fields incorrectly or treat newlines as separate records. This leads to corrupted variables and potential failures in the AI judge or SQL queries.
> 
> To fix this, sanitize the content in the SQL query inside `_prune_ai_judged` by replacing newlines and pipes with spaces, for example:
> 
> ```sql
> replace(replace(replace(substr(l.content, 1, 300), char(10), ' '), char(13), ' '), '|', ' ')
> ```
> 
> Alternatively, use `db -json` and `jq` to parse the output safely.
> 
> <details>
> <summary>References</summary>
> 
> 1. In shell scripts, the `read` command's delimiter (set via `IFS`) should always match the delimiter of the input data to ensure correct parsing.
> </details>

title: merge-stuck: pulse merge throughput collapse (5 consecutive zero-progress cycles)
body:
<!-- merge-stuck:zero-progress -->
## What

The pulse deterministic merge pass has had **5 consecutive cycles** with eligible-unmerged PRs but zero merges. The threshold is `AIDEVOPS_MERGE_ZERO_PROGRESS_CYCLES=5`.

## Why

Eligible-unmerged means `APPROVED + MERGEABLE + !draft + !hold-for-review`. When this is non-zero AND the merge count is zero across multiple cycles, the merge pass is structurally blocked — gates failing closed (e.g. branch-protection 404 mis-fire), GraphQL exhaustion, repo-allowlist mismatch, or a regression in the merge gates themselves.

## How

### Files Scope

Investigation only — no `Files Scope` declared.

### Snapshot

```
eligible_unmerged_this_cycle=1, eligible_stuck_count=0, zero_progress_cycles=5
```

### Investigation steps

1. Read `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` since the meta-issue was filed (`grep 'Merge pass: skipping' `) — the per-PR skip reason is logged for every cycle.
2. Cross-check `pulse-stats.json` for circuit-breaker fires and the `pulse_merge_branchprotect_404_skips` counter — if non-zero, the t2922 fail-closed path is mis-firing.
3. Reproduce the merge gate decision for one stuck PR via `pulse-diagnose-helper.sh pr <N>` — it explains what the pulse decided and why.
4. Apply the fix (often a one-line gate adjustment) and verify the next cycle drops zero-progress to 0.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Root cause of the throughput collapse identified.
- [ ] At least one of the stuck PRs successfully auto-merges.
- [ ] `pulse_merge_zero_progress_cycles` reads 0 in `pulse-stats.json`.

## Session Origin

Filed automatically by `pulse-merge-stuck.sh` (t3193). The detector resets the zero-progress counter on any successful merge — if the meta-issue is stale (cause already resolved), close it manually.

<sub>Source: pulse-merge-stuck-detector. Threshold env: `AIDEVOPS_MERGE_ZERO_PROGRESS_CYCLES=5`.</sub>

title: Fix postflight check-run ARG_MAX failure
body:
## Goal

Prevent postflight release verification from exceeding hosted-runner argument limits when paginated check-run responses contain large output payloads.

## Evidence

The v3.32.89 postflight run failed in `Verify CI/CD Status` with `/usr/bin/jq: Argument list too long`. `.github/workflows/postflight.yml` passes complete effective and descendant check-run arrays through `jq --argjson`, placing the API payloads in argv.

## Scope

- `.github/workflows/postflight.yml`
- `.github/scripts/reconcile-superseded-cancellations.jq`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-postflight-check-run-dedup.sh`

## Implementation Pattern

Stream JSON documents through file descriptors with jq `--slurpfile`; do not place API response payloads in command arguments. Preserve cancelled-check reconciliation semantics.

## Done When

- postflight reconciliation accepts large check-run payloads without `ARG_MAX` failure
- cancellation reconciliation and pagination regressions pass
- ShellCheck, shfmt, actionlint, and changed-file linters pass
- the fix is merged and a subsequent patch release postflight succeeds

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-postflight-check-run-dedup.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-postflight-no-source-rescan.sh`
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/tests/test-postflight-check-run-dedup.sh`
- `shfmt -d .agents/scripts/tests/test-postflight-check-run-dedup.sh`

title: Interactive full-loop should retain session ownership and reviews should state recommendations
body:
## Description

An observed interactive workflow failure exposed three related harness ambiguities:

1. `/review-issue-pr` summarized an assessment as `Approved`, which reads as exercised maintainer authority rather than a recommendation.
2. A user-requested interactive full-loop was allowed to hand implementation to a background worker even though no background worker was requested.
3. The always-loaded harness does not state strongly enough that observed failures, efficiency losses, and productivity lessons should be fixed in the current session when safely in scope, or filed as dedicated issues when larger.

## Root Cause

The review output template uses verdict nouns (`Approved / Needs Changes / Decline`) rather than recommendation language. Interactive full-loop guidance promises continuity but does not make primary-session ownership from the authorizing user turn explicit. `interactive-start-helper.sh` always passes `--background`, making asynchronous execution the default despite the conversational intent rule. Session-learning guidance exists in `reference/self-improvement.md`, but the always-loaded rule does not state the same-session repair/default clearly.

## Files to modify

- `.agents/workflows/review-issue-pr.md`: make assessment output explicitly `Recommendation: Approve / Request Changes / Decline`; reserve `Approved` for actual authority actions.
- `.agents/workflows/triage-review.md` and `.agents/scripts/pulse-ancillary-dispatch.sh`: keep the sandboxed review prompt and its deterministic prefetch template on the same recommendation contract.
- `.agents/AGENTS.md`: state that interactive full-loop remains owned and executed by the primary session from the authorizing user turn unless the user explicitly requests a background worker; add the same-session learning/repair rule with issue routing for larger work.
- `.agents/reference/task-lifecycle.md` and `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md`: detail foreground-default interactive ownership and explicit background opt-in.
- `.agents/scripts/interactive-start-helper.sh` and `.agents/scripts/tests/test-interactive-start-helper.sh`: make background startup opt-in and preserve the local-only marker in both foreground and explicitly asynchronous modes.
- `.agents/reference/self-improvement.md`: clarify immediate repair versus separately tracked larger work.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Review assessments consistently present recommendations, not completed approval claims.
- An interactive full-loop remains in the primary conversation by default; only explicit user background-worker intent permits delegation.
- The interactive start helper defaults to foreground and has tested explicit background behavior.
- The main harness requires evidence-backed session failures and efficiency/productivity lessons to be repaired immediately when safely in scope, otherwise deduplicated and filed as dedicated issues.
- Progressive-disclosure no-regression evidence, focused helper tests, ShellCheck, and local linters pass; pre-existing checker drift is tracked separately in #27492.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-interactive-start-helper.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-triage-output-shape.sh`
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/interactive-start-helper.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-ancillary-dispatch.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-interactive-start-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/progressive-load-check.sh` (compare with `main`; stale baseline failures are #27492)
- `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed`

## Scope

Keep this focused on wording and the interactive-start default. Do not redesign the full-loop state machine or worker dispatcher.

title: tier telemetry never records worker success — zero pass-rate data for optimize-tiers
body:
## Description

Tier dispatch telemetry shows 7,591 pending dispatches, 31 escalations, and **0 successes**. The success recording path is completely missing from the worker completion flow, making tier pass-rate analysis impossible.

## Expected Behavior

When a worker completes successfully, `dispatch-ledger-helper.sh record-outcome` should be called with `--outcome success` to update `tier-telemetry.jsonl`, enabling `/optimize-tiers report` to show accurate pass rates by tier.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```bash
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/dispatch-ledger-helper.sh tier-report
```

**Actual output**:

```
=== Tier Dispatch Telemetry ===
Total dispatches: 7622
Success: 0
Escalated: 31
Failed: 0

By tier:
   4447 
   2713 standard
    290 thinking
    109 bundle
     52 simple
     11 thinking (opus-4.6)

Escalation reasons:
     27 watchdog_stall_killed
      4 stale_timeout

Pass rate by tier:
  tier:simple — 0/52 (0.0%)
  tier:standard — 0/2713 (0.0%)
```

**Expected output**:

```
Success: 7560
Pass rate by tier:
  tier:simple — 48/52 (92.3%)
  tier:standard — 2680/2713 (98.8%)
```

**Causal code**:

The escalation path correctly calls `record-outcome`:

```bash
# worker-lifecycle-common.sh:1643-1646
"$ledger_helper" record-outcome \
    --issue "$issue_number" --repo "$repo_slug" \
    --outcome "escalated" --tier "$current_tier" \
    --reason "$safe_reason" 2>/dev/null || true
```

But `_hrw_finish_success_run` in `headless-runtime-worker.sh:1250-1302` releases the claim without recording the outcome:

```bash
# headless-runtime-worker.sh:1294-1299
if [[ "$release_needed" -eq 1 ]]; then
    # pr_exists or fail-open: normal success path. Post CLAIM_RELEASED with
    # reason=worker_complete so the audit trail shows the full lifecycle even
    # when no PR was created.
    _release_dispatch_claim "$session_key" "$_HRW_REASON_WORKER_COMPLETE"
fi
# ← missing: record-outcome success call here
```

**Call-site sweep**:

```bash
$ grep -c '"outcome":"success"' ~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp/tier-telemetry.jsonl
0

$ grep -c '"outcome":"pending"' ~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp/tier-telemetry.jsonl
7591

$ grep -c '"outcome":"escalated"' ~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp/tier-telemetry.jsonl
31
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run any worker dispatch that completes successfully
2. Check `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp/tier-telemetry.jsonl`
3. Observe outcome remains `"pending"` — never updated to `"success"`
4. Run `dispatch-ledger-helper.sh tier-report`
5. Observe "Success: 0"

## Proposed Fix

Add success telemetry recording to `headless-runtime-worker.sh::_hrw_finish_success_run` after line 1298:

```bash
if [[ "$release_needed" -eq 1 ]]; then
    _release_dispatch_claim "$session_key" "$_HRW_REASON_WORKER_COMPLETE"
    
    # Record success in tier telemetry
    local ledger_helper="${HOME}/.aidevops/agents/scripts/dispatch-ledger-helper.sh"
    if [[ -x "$ledger_helper" && -n "${WORKER_ISSUE_NUMBER:-}" && -n "${DISPATCH_REPO_SLUG:-}" ]]; then
        "$ledger_helper" record-outcome \
            --issue "$WORKER_ISSUE_NUMBER" \
            --repo "$DISPATCH_REPO_SLUG" \
            --outcome "success" \
            --tier "${DISPATCH_TIER:-}" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
fi
```

## Impact

- `/optimize-tiers report` cannot show pass rates (shows 0% for all tiers)
- Brief template optimization loop has no baseline to measure improvement against
- No visibility into which tiers are actually succeeding vs escalating

- **aidevops version**: 3.32.92

- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS

title: Worker failure recovery mistakes draft checkpoint PRs for completed handoffs
body:
## Description

When a headless worker terminates after creating an early draft PR, aidevops can classify that draft checkpoint as completed output, release the issue claim as `worker_complete`, and leave the incomplete draft without a bounded continuation or explicit escalation path.

This conflates three distinct states:

1. **Durability** — a draft PR preserves committed progress.
2. **Liveness** — a worker or repair process is actively advancing it.
3. **Completion** — verified output is ready for review/merge or has been explicitly escalated.

A draft PR proves durability, not completion.

In an anonymised incident on a private managed repository, the worker created the required early draft PR, continued implementation, and was then killed by the watchdog. Tests passed, but at least one requested finding remained unresolved and review identified a regression. Failure recovery discovered the existing PR, released the claim as `worker_complete`, and left the PR in draft with no subsequent continuation or escalation.

## Expected Behavior

When a worker terminates with an incomplete draft checkpoint, the draft should remain durable without being treated as completion evidence. It should have a deterministic next state: safe continuation from the preserved work or explicit escalation that leaves the objective visibly open.

The framework should avoid losing committed progress, automatically promoting partial work, starting a competing implementation, or unintentionally resuming human-held drafts.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

The failure was observed during an automated pulse dispatch for a worker-managed issue. Repository and issue identifiers are omitted because the source repository is private. The relevant lifecycle path is equivalent to:

```bash
headless-runtime-helper.sh run issue-N --repo owner/private-repository
```

The worker created an early draft PR, was watchdog-killed before satisfying all acceptance criteria, and entered failure recovery with that PR still open and draft.

**Actual output**:

Sanitised lifecycle evidence from the observing session:

```text
[lifecycle] worker_failure_recovered_existing_pr session=issue-N branch=worker-branch
[claim] released session=issue-N reason=worker_complete
```

Subsequent inspection showed:

```text
PR state: OPEN
Draft: true
Requested work: incomplete
Active continuation worker: none
Explicit escalation: none
```

**Expected output**:

The draft should be recorded as durable progress, but the issue should not be reported as completed solely because the PR exists. The framework should select a safe continuation or escalation state without discarding the remaining objective.

**Causal code**:

Current `main` at aidevops v3.32.93 still contains the relevant state reductions:

```text
2bbdcea392 .agents/scripts/shared-claim-lifecycle.sh:181  _pr_exists_for_branch_or_issue()
7c6dccaf1a .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh:859 _recover_worker_output_on_failure()
4a93b84708 .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-stale.sh:500 _recover_stale_assignment()
4a93b84708 .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-pr.sh:177 _has_open_pr_check_open_body_keyword()
```

Commit `4c9d1984a` introduced standard early draft creation and durable-progress preservation. Parts of the completion and dedup behaviour predate that change, so it appears to expose an interaction rather than being the sole source of the defect.

**Call-site sweep**:

The relevant symbols occur in:

```text
.agents/scripts/shared-claim-lifecycle.sh
.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh
.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh
.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-stale.sh
.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-pr.sh
.agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-output-classification-head-vs-search.sh
.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-helper.sh
.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-dedup-stale-terminal-evidence.sh
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Dispatch a managed issue to a headless worker.
2. Let the worker make a coherent first commit and create the protocol-required draft PR.
3. Terminate the worker after the draft is pushed but before all acceptance criteria are complete.
4. Allow `_recover_worker_output_on_failure` and post-worker handoff processing to inspect the branch.
5. Observe that finding an existing PR can lead to `worker_complete` even though the PR remains draft.
6. Observe that open-PR dedup/stale-recovery paths preserve the checkpoint but do not establish a bounded continuation or explicit escalation state.

## Analysis and Contributing Code Paths

The observed result appears to arise because several lifecycle paths reduce PR state to “a PR exists” without retaining whether it is draft, ready, merged, or closed:

- `.agents/scripts/shared-claim-lifecycle.sh`
  - `_pr_exists_for_branch_or_issue` returns `found|absent|unknown`, discarding `state` and `isDraft`.
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh`
  - `_recover_worker_output_on_failure` treats a discovered PR as recovered output and releases the claim with `worker_complete`.
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh`
  - `_worker_post_pr_handoff_confirmed` can accept an open PR after a hard-killed worker without distinguishing a draft checkpoint.
- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-stale.sh`
  - Stale recovery preserves ownership whenever an open PR exists, but does not appear to establish a subsequent continuation or escalation transition.
- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-pr.sh`
  - The closing-keyword path fetches `number,body`, so it cannot distinguish a draft from a ready PR.

Parts of this behaviour predate early draft creation. Commit `4c9d1984a` appears to have exposed the interaction by making early draft PRs the standard worker durability mechanism; it should not necessarily be treated as the sole source of the defect.

There may also be inconsistent draft semantics between dedup paths: an existing test expects draft sibling PRs not to block one path, while closing-keyword detection can still block them.

These are candidate contributing paths rather than a prescribed location for the fix.

## Design Considerations

Any solution may need to preserve these properties:

- Early draft PRs remain durable checkpoints.
- Draft existence alone is not completion evidence.
- Partial drafts are not automatically promoted to ready.
- Recovery continues from the existing PR head rather than accidentally starting from the default branch.
- Concurrent workers do not advance the same checkpoint.
- Retries are bounded and exhaustion becomes explicit escalation.
- Human-created, interactive, or intentionally held drafts are not resumed automatically.
- Ready and merged PRs retain their existing lifecycle behaviour.
- Generic dispatch deduplication is not weakened in a way that creates competing branches.

The existing exact-head PR repair machinery in `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-feedback.sh` may contain reusable primitives for leases, bounded attempts, linked worktrees, and stale recovery. Reusing or extracting those primitives is one possible approach, but maintainers are better placed to decide whether continuation belongs there or in the worker lifecycle itself.

Questions the implementation should resolve include:

1. What state distinguishes a durable draft checkpoint from a completed handoff?
2. Which component owns continuation after the original worker terminates?
3. How is eligibility limited to verified worker-managed drafts?
4. How should active continuation, exhaustion, explicit holds, and maintainer-review states interact with dispatch deduplication?
5. Which PR state should be authoritative across recovery, stale assignment, and completion reporting?

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A terminal worker with an incomplete draft PR is not reported as successfully completed solely because the PR exists.
- [ ] The preserved draft has a deterministic next state: safe continuation or explicit escalation.
- [ ] Recovery does not lose committed progress or accidentally continue from the default branch.
- [ ] Recovery cannot create overlapping workers or competing implementations.
- [ ] Retry or continuation behaviour is bounded.
- [ ] Drafts are not automatically marked ready without completion evidence.
- [ ] Human-created, interactive, explicitly held, and maintainer-gated drafts are not resumed unintentionally.
- [ ] Ready and merged PRs retain correct monitoring and completion behaviour.
- [ ] Draft semantics are consistent across failure recovery, stale recovery, and dispatch deduplication.
- [ ] Regression tests cover worker termination with an open draft, successful recovery, exhausted recovery, explicit holds, ready PRs, and merged PRs.

## Workarounds Applied

No production workaround was applied. The affected draft, issue, labels, and repository files were left unchanged during investigation.

Manually marking the draft ready was rejected because implementation was incomplete. Fresh ordinary redispatch was rejected because it would not guarantee continuation from the exact existing PR head.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.32.93
- **Latest version**: 3.32.93
- **Install method**: unknown
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21
- **Working repo**: aidevops (`main`)
- **gh CLI**: 2.96.0

## Additional Context

Recent duplicate searches found related closed work concerning session continuation, dirty worktree recovery, and exact-head CI repair, but no issue covering the specific transition from a terminal worker plus an incomplete open draft to false completion with no continuation owner.

No private repository name, URL, issue number, PR number, branch name, or local path is included in this report.

title: Prevent duplicate deterministic merge completion summaries across pulse runners
body:
Problem: Two deterministic pulse runners posted the same completion summary to one private downstream PR eight seconds apart after merge; private evidence is retained in the originating interactive session. title: Replace provider-specific manual dispatch guidance with tier-based routing
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `tier model routing documentation` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons.
- [x] Discovery pass: PR #27060 established provider-neutral workload tiers; no open PR addresses this guidance.
- [x] File refs verified: command guidance and helper help/error locations exist at HEAD.
- [x] Tier: `tier:thinking` — this edits a self-hosting dispatch-path helper.
- [x] Seeded draft PR: skipped — issue-only avoids collision with active #27501 work.

## What

Replace provider-specific model recommendations in manual single-issue dispatch documentation, CLI help/errors, examples, and tests with canonical `simple`, `standard`, or `thinking` workload-tier guidance. Runtime routing must choose the preferred available provider, model, and reasoning level.

## Why

Current guidance recommends a concrete Anthropic model even when installations use another provider. This contradicts the provider-neutral routing contract merged in PR #27060 and can direct operators to unavailable models.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:thinking`

**Tier rationale:** The change is bounded, but `.agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh` is a self-hosting dispatch-path file.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/commands/dispatch-issue.md:10,46-56,73-84` — make tiers the recommended interface and examples.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh:224-275,919-935,1470-1520` — align help/errors/examples; retain explicit model override only as an advanced compatibility escape hatch if still supported.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh` and/or `.agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-model-tiers.sh` — prevent provider-specific recommendations from returning.
- REVIEW: `.agents/reference/worker-diagnostics.md:76` and `.agents/reference/configuration.md:150-160` for the same recommendation pattern.

### Complete Write Surface

- Readers: command markdown, CLI help, validation errors, and reference examples.
- Writers/schema/migrations: N/A; guidance only.
- Tests: focused dispatch-helper and canonical-tier policy suites.
- Deployment: `.agents/` is canonical; deploy through `setup.sh`, never by editing the installed mirror.

### Implementation Steps

1. Inventory provider/model IDs presented as manual-dispatch recommendations.
2. Replace recommendations with workload tiers and runtime-routing language.
3. Preserve intentionally supported explicit model overrides as advanced compatibility behavior only.
4. Add regression coverage keeping docs, help, and errors synchronized.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- Do not break existing automation that deliberately passes `--model <id>` without first proving that override obsolete.
- Do not substitute a different hard-coded provider; preferences change over time.
- No concurrency or migration hazard; reverting restores prior guidance.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-model-tiers.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh
git grep -n -E "anthropic/claude-opus|openai/|google/" -- .agents/scripts/commands/dispatch-issue.md .agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh
```

Any retained provider match must be a justified compatibility fixture or factual routing example, not a recommendation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Manual-dispatch guidance recommends canonical workload tiers, not a provider/model ID.
- [ ] Runtime routing remains authoritative for provider, model, and reasoning preferences.
- [ ] Explicit model overrides, if retained, are marked as advanced compatibility behavior.
- [ ] Command docs, CLI help/errors, and tests agree.
- [ ] Regression coverage rejects provider-specific recommendation examples.

title: Keep OpenCode session, Tabby tab, and release-version titles synchronized
body:
## Description

OpenCode session renames can append an older aidevops version than the current deployed release, and Tabby tabs can retain a different title from the authoritative OpenCode session.

## Reproducer

A live session-rename after updating to aidevops 3.32.93 produced AIDevOps 3.32.88. The active OpenCode process retained a stale AIDEVOPS_VERSION; the plugin passes its immutable startup bundle to title-version readers; an existing generated OpenCode Tabby profile has disableDynamicTitle true; and the plugin skips terminal-title emission when an event already has the expected suffix.

## Expected Behavior

The active deployed VERSION is the source for newly written suffixes. Every meaningful OpenCode title update or reload reasserts the complete same title to the terminal, and managed OpenCode Tabby profiles permit dynamic titles.

## Worker Guidance

### Files to Modify

.opencode/lib/session-title-suffix.ts; .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs; .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-title-suffix.mjs and tests; .agents/scripts/session-rename-helper.sh and tests if stale precedence is confirmed; .agents/scripts/tabby-profile-sync.py; tests/test-tabby-profile-sync.py.

### Implementation Steps

Separate immutable runtime-code resolution from live deployed-version resolution; prefer active deployed VERSION over process-start environment and stale repository copies with safe development fallbacks. Re-emit canonical meaningful titles even when no API rewrite is needed, including restore events without loops. Set disableDynamicTitle false for new and existing aidevops-managed OpenCode profiles while preserving unrelated profiles. Add regression tests for stale version sources, idempotent title synchronization, restored sessions, and profile repair.

### Hazards and Compatibility

Preserve immutable runtime code bundles and leases; only live version metadata follows deployment. Keep OSC writes best-effort and sanitized. Do not rewrite arbitrary Tabby profiles.

### Verification Before Dispatch

Run targeted Node or Bun title tests, shell title tests, Python Tabby tests, ShellCheck for changed shell files, and repository local linters.

## Workarounds Applied

None; the mismatch was independently reproduced and Tabby configuration inspected without mutation.

title: Prevent runtime-readable artifacts from using host /tmp
body:
Problem: OpenCode correctly treats host /tmp as external; a session wrote a complexity report there and stalled when Read requested approval. Root cause: managed launchers redirect generic temp variables but expose no named aidevops temp variable, always-loaded guidance does not prohibit explicit /tmp paths for runtime-readable artifacts, and Browser QA plus operational examples reinforce the unsafe path. Implementation: export AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR from .agents/scripts/shared-temp-workspace.sh; add concise guidance in .agents/AGENTS.md; move Browser QA and milestone defaults; update operational examples; extend test-managed-temp-workspace.sh.
